newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia vegetable oil, sugar seen in surplus.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia vegetable oil, sugar seen in surplus.

text.p: Yugoslavia will produce enough vegetable oil and sugar to meet domestic needs for a year and leave a surplus for export, Belgrade daily Politika reported on Friday.
"Domestic production of oil and sugar will meet one year's home needs and there will be surpluses for export," Todo Vasilic of the Novi Sad industrial crops business community was quoted as saying.
The 159,000 hectares under sunflower this year were expected to yield 351,000 tonnes of seed, with the 67,000 ha under soy giving 134,000 tonnes of beans.
Crop output would be enough to produce 159,000 tonnes of vegetable oil.
"This will meet one year's needs of our consumers... and we also have 50,000 tonnes of last year's oil reserves so we will have a surplus of this staple," said Vasilic.
Some 56,000 ha under sugar beet were expected to yield around 200,000 tonnes of sugar, he said.
Imports made earlier had increased stocks and cut sales of domestic sugar.
One of the problems faced by producers was late payment by the state.
Some producers were still owed for last year's sunflower, soybean and sugar beet crops, he said.
"We are already considering how we will sell this year's crop since the market is saturated," Vasilic said.

Prices of these products were below production costs, which was another reason why primary producers might be reluctant to sell new crops to manufacturers. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
